svg.title: Blameless Postmortems
svg.desc: Blameless Postmortems. Learn from every incident without blame: a timeline, the contributing factors and tracked action items, shared widely. Step 1, Blame stops the learning: “Who pushed the deploy?” One engineer is blamed, people hide mistakes, and 6 weeks later it recurs. Step 2, A blameless postmortem: Within 5 working days the people involved rebuild what happened: 4 contributing factors, no culprit. Step 3, Follow up and share: A facilitated review, 4 owned and dated items (3 done by 21 Oct) and a lesson every team can find. Step 4, Common pitfalls: Blameless isn't consequence-free; ‘human error’, one root cause or items that never close stall it.

g.text: “Who pushed the deploy?” One engineer is blamed, people hide mistakes, and 6 weeks later it recurs.
Within 5 working days the people involved rebuild what happened: 4 contributing factors, no culprit.
A facilitated review, 4 owned and dated items (3 done by 21 Oct) and a lesson every team can find.
Blameless isn't consequence-free; ‘human error’, one root cause or items that never close stall it.
Mon 5 Oct · by a manager · shared with 3 people
the engineer should have tested it
so the next team gets no warning
SEV-2 · Sat 3 Oct · by Mai, Tom and Ploy
no data loss, no double charges
went from 3 s to 30 s in 1.43.0
and p95 on the main path
A new 30 s default timeout met a
roles set 3 min after the page
a Saturday evening, not a sale
on a 30 s default: the same failure
One root cause, or human error
stops the learning: keep all four
factors, ask why it made sense
